title: Chipsi mayai (Tanzanian chips omelette)

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and cut in thin fries
oil for frying, plus 2 tbsp for the omelette
kachumbari (tomato and onion salad) and hot sauce, to serve

steps: Deep-fry or oven-bake the fries until golden and tender; drain and season lightly.
Beat the eggs with the onion, tomato, salt and pepper.
Heat the 2 tablespoons of oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Tip in the fries, spread them out, and pour the eggs over, tilting the pan.
Cook for 3 minutes until the base is set, then flip using a plate and cook the other side 2 to 3 minutes until golden.
Cut into wedges and serve with kachumbari and hot sauce.

title: Kuku paka (Tanzanian coconut chicken curry)
steps: Marinate the chicken with the lemon juice, half the garlic, ginger, salt, and half the curry powder for 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken until charred on the outside; it does not need to cook through.
Heat the oil in a pot, cook the onion for 6 minutes, then add the remaining garlic, ginger, curry powder, turmeric and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Pour in the coconut milk and chilli, add the chicken, and simmer gently for 25 minutes until cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Scatter with coriander and serve with rice or chapati.

title: Mandazi (Tanzanian cardamom and coconut fried dough)
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar, cardamom and salt.
Whisk the coconut milk, egg and butter, then pour into the dry ingredients and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll out to about 1 cm thick and cut into triangles or squares.
Fry in oil at about 170 C for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain and serve warm with tea.

title: Mtori (Tanzanian green banana and beef soup)

ingredients.name: beef on the bone, in pieces
green cooking bananas or green plantains, peeled and cut up

steps: Cook the beef in the water with half the onion and salt for 45 to 60 minutes until tender.
Fry the remaining onion in the oil, add the tomatoes and cook to a thick sauce; add to the pot.
Add the bananas (and potatoes if using) and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until falling apart.
Take out the meat, mash the bananas in the broth with a masher, or blend until the stew is thick and smooth.
Return the beef, stir in the milk, and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Taste and season, then serve hot.

title: Sukuma wiki (East African braised collard greens)

ingredients.name: collard greens or kale, stems removed, thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oil and fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Add the greens in batches, stirring so they wilt.
Pour in the water, add salt, cover, and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Uncover and cook off any liquid, then serve with ugali or rice.

title: Ugali (Tanzanian stiff maize meal porridge)
steps: Bring 600 ml of the water to a boil in a heavy saucepan with the salt.
Mix the flour with the remaining water to a smooth paste and stir into the boiling water to form a loose porridge.
Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the remaining flour a handful at a time, beating with a wooden spoon, until the mixture is thick and pulls away from the pot.
Cover and cook on low for 5 minutes, then stir vigorously for 3 minutes more.
Shape into a mound with a wet spoon and serve hot with stew or greens, eaten by hand.
